baseCamp.heroLead: The future operational, logistics, training and experience hub where NÓMADA EXTREMO adventures, workshops, retreats and experiences would begin.
baseCamp.heroText: A base to prepare every outing with precision. A hangar to protect equipment. A school to train safely. A fleet ready to move between coast, mountains and desert. And a camp where adventure, nature, rest and community meet in one place.
baseCamp.noticeText: This section describes a future development vision for NÓMADA EXTREMO. Locations, budgets, vehicles and facilities are indicative and would depend on technical, urban, legal, financial, environmental and tourism studies.
baseCamp.visionIntro: BASE AND CAMP NÓMADA EXTREMO is the vision for a future owned infrastructure to organise, professionalise and scale the project. The main base would work as a logistics, technical and training hub; the camp would be its natural extension for multi-day experiences, retreats, community and nature.

baseCamp.faq2A: Indicatively, in an industrial or logistics area of Águilas that allows access, loading, storage and quick departures to coast and mountains.
baseCamp.faq3Q: Would it be a naturist camp?

baseCamp.faq4A: Depending on the development level, from a prudent 40,000-120,000 € phase to a complete vision requiring much larger investments.

pablo.body:
Thank you, Pablo, for teaching me to approach swimming with technical judgement and for helping me recognise real progress in the water. Through the videos, sessions and everyday pool work, I have improved enormously thanks to your trust, closeness, explanations and method.

I take with me your technical knowledge, your corrections and your ability to make every session matter. Finishing the year with an honours grade reflects everything you invested in us. Your humour, simplicity and way of connecting with the group show the great person you are and made rigour, warmth and motivation work together.
pablo.key: Technique, progress in the water, confidence and real improvement.

pepe.tag: Route Planning · Low and Mid-Mountain Guiding
pepe.body:
Thank you, Pepe, for teaching me that a route is far more than walking. With you I learned to plan, interpret, navigate, assess risk, prepare equipment, use maps and think about the group before taking a step. Your passion for the mountains and respect for the natural environment make learning from you an honour.

Thank you for your trust, your words, your closeness and that hug at the end of the first term. I hope next year I can continue learning rope manoeuvres with you, that almost magical field that opens the door to canyoning, climbing and caving, always through technique, safety and respect for the mountain.
pepe.key: Planning, navigation, mountains, safety and respect for the natural environment.

mariano.body:
Thank you, Mariano, for being much more than a teacher: you are someone I feel could be a lifelong friend. I take with me the routes, conversations, adjustments and trust, and your way of turning cycling and the aquatic environment into technique, effort, teamwork and joy.

I have learned so much from your attention to detail and your insistence on preparation and good information. I am delighted that next year we will meet again in Biological Foundations for Activities in the Natural Environment. I hope we keep learning and sharing adventures, including that pending night snorkel.
mariano.key: Cycling, aquatic environment, preparation, teamwork and trust.

nacho.body:
Thank you, Nacho, for making learning feel close, natural and enjoyable. Your rapport with everyone, your jokes, your way of teaching and your support for the group have left a very special memory.

I take with me your kindness, effort, trust in me and your ability to make every class more human and easier to experience. With you, learning comes through closeness and commitment, while always paying attention to the group. If the path continues that way, we will meet again next year in rope work, and I am really looking forward to it.
nacho.key: Group support, closeness, trust, communication and guidance.

antonio.tag: Official Tutor · Cycling · Aquatic Natural Environment
antonio.body:
Thank you, Antonio: discovering you as a teacher has been wonderful. I love how you communicate, teach and turn every second of class or practice into genuine learning. Thank you for your empathy, closeness, your words on the beach and everything learned in cycling, the aquatic environment, safety and group work.

I especially enjoyed the school visits and bicycle circuits with the children; their excitement and affection made me feel like one of them. I now have a clear foundation for next year. I sincerely hope you teach us again: continuing to learn and share practices, outings and experiences with you would be a privilege.
antonio.key: Cycling, aquatic environment, safety, empathy and practical learning.

samuel.tag: Tutor and Teacher · First Stage of the Course
samuel.body:
Thank you, Samuel. It was a great pleasure to have you as tutor and teacher during the first part of the year. Your warmth, friendliness and positive way of facing every situation left a very good mark on the group.

Although the course later moved into a different stage, I remember your humour, clear explanations and the confidence you brought to our lessons and outings. I hope everything is going very well for you and that you keep sharing that positive way of being with people.
samuel.key: Closeness, a positive atmosphere, trust and a constructive attitude.

puli.body:
Thank you, Puli. You taught me my first muscle-up at Royal Box, and this year you also introduced me to a special side of digitalisation, giving me the chance to grow further in the digital world. I had a great time with you and learned a lot.

This website also comes from that mixture of technique, trust, creativity and the desire to build something of my own. Thank you, mate. Always stay true to yourself, because your energy, authenticity and natural ability to connect with people also teach us.
puli.key: Digitalisation, creativity, trust and personal development.

juana.body:
Thank you, Juana Mari, for everything you have taught me. It has been an enormous and, above all, highly practical learning experience for everyday life and the workplace. I loved your effective, clear and approachable way of teaching; you are a wonderful teacher.

I take with me employment rights and duties, risk prevention, first aid, contracts, employability, personal skills and a more thoughtful way of building a professional project. Thank you for making such an important subject feel practical, close and genuinely useful.
juana.key: Employability, prevention, labour rights, first aid and a professional project.

beatriz.body:
Thank you, Beatriz, for being a wonderful teacher. I learned many things that will help us professionally, especially when working with people from abroad and communicating clearly, politely and safely. As someone who loves English, having you as my teacher was a real joy.

I take with me vocabulary for equipment, sports, health, injuries, presentations and customer service, as well as a more professional way to communicate. I hope everything goes brilliantly in your future projects. Thank you for making a subject I already loved even more special.
beatriz.key: Professional communication, technical vocabulary, customer service and applied English.

alberto.body:
Thank you, Alberto. We have seen less of each other and spoken more towards the end of the final term, but it is easy to see that you are a first-rate person with a big heart. Your passion for nature, travel and everything you do is equally clear.

I value your calm, approachable way of being with the group and the feeling that there is still so much to learn from you. See you next year in horse riding, Alberto! I am genuinely excited to spend more time with you and continue learning in a new discipline.
alberto.key: Nature, travel, closeness, horse riding and the desire to keep learning.

october.work1: Nómada Extremo’s team leads sea and mountain experiences, interpretive walks and outdoor leisure activities from our base in Águilas.
october.work2: For technical disciplines, the model provides for a qualified partner specialist centre for each activity, with its professionals, equipment and procedures. Selection is made for each experience.
october.work3Title: Growing with our own base and resources
october.work3: In the long term, Horizonte Nómada envisages our own base and resources for the most in-demand lines: a base, camp, fleet or certified school. Growth follows demand and the viability of each line.

october.mixed: Mountain biking: Nómada staff. Canyoning and rafting: partner specialist centre.
october.intro: Nómada Extremo’s business plan defines a responsible role for each activity family. Disciplines led by our own team are part of the Nómada staff; more technical ones are delivered with partner specialist centres qualified in each discipline. Every experience requires qualified professionals, liability and accident insurance, permits where applicable, emergency procedures and equipment checks. Adventure is at the heart of what we do, but safety sets the limit.
october.scope1: Leads mountain routes and prepares the group. Coordinates climbing, via ferratas and technical abseiling with a partner specialist centre.
october.scope4: Leads sea kayaking, paddleboarding and snorkelling, interprets the coast and adapts routes to the group. Coordinates coasteering with a partner specialist centre.
october.divingMeaning: SSI Open Water Instructor is the training reference for teaching recreational diving within its scope. React Right provides emergency response training. Current authorisation, the centre, insurance and procedures are checked before each experience.
october.qualificationMeaning: Indicative training is checked against the role’s responsibilities and the specific activity. Current qualifications, scope of practice, insurance, permits and emergency response capability must be verified.

october.quote: "How I am when I’m alone with myself is one thing; being responsible for a group of people is quite another. Then there is nothing to prove: just prepare, look after everyone and bring everyone back."
october.schoolRoles: Mountain, canyoning, mountain biking and navigation roles according to the activity
october.naturistCoordinator: The naturist experiences and outdoor wellbeing coordinator manages the briefing, privacy, pace and immediate response to any discomfort, without directing the experience in an intrusive way.
october.duty2: Teaches try-dives and SSI courses, leads dives and prepares the safety briefing.
october.duty3: Coordinates flights and jumps, assesses weather and checks passenger readiness.
october.duty5: Leads mountain biking and coordinates canyoning and rafting with the specialist centre. Plans routes and progression.
october.duty6: Teaches foil and board sports, adapts sessions and supervises equipment.
october.duty7: Plans filming, coordinates drone flights and edits content without disrupting the activity.
october.duty8: Leads cave routes, organises rope progression and protects cave environments.
october.duty9: Installs and checks jumping systems, prepares participants and controls the operation.
october.duty10: Operates the vessel, coordinates parasailing and supervises boarding, towing and recovery.
october.duty11: Coordinates naturist experiences and wellbeing, protects privacy and adapts the pace to the group.
october.duty12: Teaches navigation and outdoor self-reliance, plans practical sessions and applies minimal-impact principles.
october.risk1: Checked equipment and systems, adapted ratios, weather assessment and an evacuation plan.
october.risk2: Briefing, air and depth checks, buddy pairs, emergency oxygen and sea and equipment assessment.
october.risk3: Wind, take-off and landing areas, equipment and passenger checked. Postponed without a safe operating margin.
october.risk4: Wind, waves, currents and exits checked; buoyancy equipment, communication and alternative return prepared.
october.risk5: Flow, weather, escape routes and group level checked, with continuous monitoring and withdrawal alternatives.
october.risk6: Area, depth, wind and traffic monitored; helmet, vest, battery and rescue point checked.
october.risk7: Permits, flight areas and image consent checked. Group safety takes priority over the shot.
october.risk8: Access, flood risk, backup lighting, ropes, communication and exit procedure checked.
october.risk9: Anchors and redundant systems double-checked, participant readiness verified, evacuation and weather assessed.
october.risk10: Vessel and tow equipment checked, permits and insurance verified, with conservative cancellation for wind or sea conditions.
october.risk11: Small groups, consent, privacy and respect; immediate response to discomfort or inappropriate behaviour.
october.risk12: Route, water, weather and escape routes checked; emergency equipment, permits and environmental protection planned.
october.complementaryIntro: Jumping and parasailing are coordinated with partner specialist centres. Naturist experiences, wellbeing, navigation and survival are covered by Nómada staff roles.
